system.description:
Quietus, the Assamites claim, arose for purposes beyond pure combat. By ritually bathing a willing subject in his own blood, an Assamite can purge that subject's mind of most supernatural influences. It is most often used on Assamites returning to Alamut after long sojourns abroad, to confirm they have not been turned against the clan.

The character touches the subject and spends Blood Traits equal to the target's Willpower. The subject makes a Static Mental Challenge (retest Willpower) against a difficulty of 3 Traits plus the level of the power in question for each outside mental or emotional influence he is under (difficulty 7 Traits if the influence has no level). Success nullifies that influence. This cannot remove effects carried by blood (including the blood bond) or purely mundane techniques such as coercion, but it can lift magical or thaumaturgical curses if the character's Quietus rating is at least equal to the level with which the curse was cast.
system.source: Libellus Sanguinis III: Wolves at the Door, Book Two
